solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Belvedere that accommodates accountant and family

parts.note: an accountant is one who sums, jokily a summer
a house is a family line, as in the House of Windsor

explanation.surface: A grand viewpoint building that houses a bookkeeper and their relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accountant' is read as one who does sums.
explanation.definitionFit: A belvedere is a garden pavilion built to enjoy a view, the same sort of building.

clue.text: A fighter for the crown in Oxford and Rye, maybe

parts.note: Oxford is a university, uni for short
rye is one example of a cereal crop, corn

explanation.surface: A contender for the throne is found in two English towns, Oxford and Rye.
explanation.walkthrough: Rye is also a town in Sussex, which is the misdirection. The nursery rhyme has the lion and the unicorn fighting for the crown.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme the heraldic beast battles the lion for the crown, both supporters on the royal arms.

clue.text: Begging from people? Sleuth finds it impossible

parts.note: men are people
a DI is a Detective Inspector, a police sleuth
one who finds it impossible can't

explanation.surface: A detective concludes that begging from passers-by cannot be done.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant friar lives on alms, so the adjective describes someone living by begging.

clue.text: One leaving service — though not with Sappers latterly — is to join up again

indicators.note: not with says the sappers' letters must be taken away from the leaver
latterly says the later occurrence of those two letters is the one removed

parts.note: someone leaving employment is a retiree
RE, the Royal Engineers, are the army's sappers

explanation.surface: A soldier quitting the forces, no longer with the engineers, plans to re-enlist.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the second RE from RETIREE leaves RETIE. 'join up again' looks military but just means tie once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie something again is to fasten or join it up once more.

clue.text: Majority of L-dopa queries becoming more puzzling

indicators.note: most of the run of letters in dopa queries is kept, so the solution sits inside the words

explanation.surface: Questions about a Parkinson's drug becoming harder to understand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Majority of' sends the solver to most of DOPAQUERIES, losing the D and the IES.
explanation.definitionFit: Something less transparent is harder to see through, so more obscure and baffling.

clue.text: Music man from Sacramento lacking credit and with no end in sight, sadly

indicators.note: sadly signals the remaining letters are in a sorry, jumbled state
no end says the final letter of what remains is dropped
lacking says the credit letters go missing from the city

parts.note: the Californian city's name taken letter for letter
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A musician from California is unhappily short of money with no relief coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes CR and 'with no end in sight' drops the final O, leaving SAAMENT; 'sadly' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedrich Smetana was the Czech composer of The Bartered Bride and Ma Vlast.

clue.text: How to make book (like Mantel?) immediately available?

definitions.meaning: taking a book off a shelf, a mantel being a shelf and Mantel a novelist, makes it available

explanation.walkthrough: Hilary Mantel is the novelist, but a mantel is also a shelf over a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold ready-made from stock rather than to order are ready to buy at once.

clue.text: Striving hard

definitions.meaning: difficult and wearing, as in a tiresome day

explanation.definitionFit: The participle means attempting, while the adjective means taxing or exasperating.

clue.text: Could be varlet going abroad?

parts.note: taken as wordplay, the solution says to make the second word strange, and doing so to its letters could give varlet

explanation.surface: A knave's servant might be heading overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read FOREIGN as an anagram signal working on TRAVEL, and the result could be VARLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Journeys to other countries are what going overseas involves.

clue.text: See 9
Filming again, eager to keep each extra quiet on emperor's entry

indicators.note: to keep means the eager word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: raring, as in raring to go, means eager

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so comes first

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very quiet

indicators.note: the entry of a word is its opening, so its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A film shoot where keen extras must stay silent when the emperor comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filming' is misleading: the definition is about coming into view once more, not cameras. The extras are pianissimo, the musical mark, rather than film extras.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing up once more, as an actor might do when shot a second time, is a return to view.

clue.text: Capital experience Colin discovered

parts.note: a trip, especially a drug trip, is an experience

indicators.note: discovered means uncovered, so the outer letters of Colin come off

explanation.surface: A man called Colin found out about a capital experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the chief city and seat of government of Libya.

clue.text: Hull 'supporter' departed for match

parts.note: Rod Hull's puppet Emu was carried on his arm, so jokily supported by him
late means dead, departed

explanation.surface: A Hull City fan left early for the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull looks like the football club, but it is Rod Hull, a British TV entertainer whose glove puppet was the aggressive bird Emu.
explanation.definitionFit: To equal or rival someone by copying them is to match them.

clue.text: Give boost via this with toast, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a breakfast item served on toast, read as two words

explanation.surface: Something that perks you up, such as a breakfast dish on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone along is to encourage them, while a fried breakfast item sits atop toast.

clue.text: Concerning Mother's parking — it's a gas!

parts.note: after can mean about or concerning, as in asking after someone
a dam is a mother animal
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Mum's parking is hilarious, a real gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's a gas' looks like slang for great fun but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Miners name the choking carbon monoxide mixture left after a firedamp explosion this way.

clue.text: 'Vessels' in title needing changing — it's a pivotal passage

indicators.note: in places the vessels inside the reworked word
needing changing says the letters of title must be altered into a new order

parts.note: urns are vessels

explanation.surface: A heading with the word vessels in it must be rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pivotal' sounds like important, but the passage literally turns on a pivot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating barrier lets people pass one at a time, turning on a central pivot.

clue.text: Cataract possibly, as usually seen twice a day at Southend?

definitions.meaning: a cataract can be a torrent or flood

definitions.text: usually seen twice a day at Southend
definitions.meaning: the peak of the tide comes in about twice daily at the Essex seaside town

explanation.surface: An eye condition that is normally visible twice daily at a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Southend-on-Sea is an Essex resort on the Thames estuary with a long pier. 'Cataract' suggests the eye condition, but here it is a deluge.
explanation.definitionFit: Flood conditions are deep water, and the term also names the top of the tide.

clue.text: Awkward situation for gourmet — freezer being regularly empty

indicators.note: emptying at regular intervals leaves only every other letter of each word

explanation.surface: A food lover is in trouble because the freezer keeps running out.
explanation.walkthrough: Odd letters of gourmet give GUMT, even letters of freezer give REE. 'Up a gum tree' is the idiom for being in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up a eucalyptus is the idiom for being stuck in a fix, so the tree stands for the predicament.

clue.text: Crushed fabric

explanation.definitionFit: The verb to worst means to defeat, and the woollen cloth takes its name from a Norfolk village.

clue.text: Avoiding Palladium, pranged Sierra

indicators.note: avoiding says those letters are left out of the crashed word

parts.note: Pd is the chemical symbol for palladium

explanation.surface: Steering clear of the London Palladium, someone crashed their Ford Sierra.
explanation.walkthrough: Sierra looks like the Ford car, a natural partner for pranged, a British slang word for crashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a jagged chain of mountains, a mountain chain.

clue.text: Gathering 11 is fruitless

indicators.note: fruitless says a fruit is taken out, here the one that grows on a tree in orchards

parts.note: the answer to 11 Down, meaning filming again

explanation.surface: A meeting about clue 11 proves unproductive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruitless' removes a fruit, PEAR, which is not printed in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Harvesting a crop is collecting it in, the gathering of the harvest.

clue.text: It offers lip service, giving up censure on family

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it
in a down clue giving up means turned upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
kin are family

explanation.surface: Someone stops criticising their relatives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lip service' usually means hollow support; here it is literal, wiping lips at table.
explanation.definitionFit: A table linen square is used for wiping the mouth, serving the lips.

clue.text: Sucker giving millions to substituted player

indicators.note: substituted means the letters are swapped around into another order

explanation.surface: A gullible person pays millions to a footballer brought on as a replacement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' suggests a dupe, but it is an eel-like fish.
explanation.definitionFit: This jawless fish clamps onto prey with a round sucking mouth.

clue.text: Country with sycophants? Not singular

indicators.note: S is short for singular, and not says it is dropped

parts.note: yes-men are sycophants

explanation.surface: A nation full of flatterers, and more than one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen is a nation at the southern tip of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Run swindle alongside immature US villain

parts.note: a scam is a swindle

indicators.note: immature means not finished, so the last letter goes

parts.note: perp is American slang for a perpetrator

explanation.surface: A con trick worked with a young American criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash off quickly with light steps is to run.

clue.text: Acting in prologue, time to enter

indicators.note: to enter says the time letter goes into the preface word

parts.note: a proem is a preface or prologue

explanation.surface: An actor in the opening scene waits for the moment to come on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acting' suggests the theatre, but it means temporary.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means for the time being, so a deputy acting in a post holds it temporarily.

clue.text: Iris's the first person free to accompany boy

parts.note: I is the first-person pronoun
to rid is to free
Ian is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A girl called Iris is the first to be released to go with a lad.
explanation.walkthrough: Iris looks like a woman's name; it is the part of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means belonging to the coloured ring of the eye, a possessive sense.

clue.text: 'Vanguard' idle — engaged with refitting

indicators.note: refitting means the letters are fitted together afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: A warship named Vanguard lies idle while undergoing a refit.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Vanguard suggests a ship in dock; the definition is the foremost position.
explanation.definitionFit: The front line of progress in a field is its forefront, the most advanced position.
